## MirKAt
We are also interested in the association between the microbiome (particularly at baseline) and outcomes (particularly change in outcomes. We will use a function called MiRKAT to analyse the microbiome as a predictor of clinical outcomes.

<br>

Does the BL microbiome predict change in clinical outcomes (% and absolute), controlling for the baseline value and other covariates?

<br>

I will have you go through the secondary outcomes of interest here (and any others that you and Maggie have disccused looking at)

### Load in data
```{r}
#load in the metadata
meta <- fread("C:/Users/jhres/Documents/DRIFT2/Week3/DRIFT_long_metadata_microbiome_092026.csv")

#and the aithison distance matrix (think this dataframe is ~495x495)
Aitchison <- fread()
```

```{r}
#prep data
#factor varaiables
#standardize alpha diversity measures


#meta <- meta %>% arrange(subject_id)

#filter metadata to timepoints of interest (e.g., BL & 3m) and arrange by SampleID so they are all in the same order
meta.0m<- meta[meta$time==0,] %>%
  arrange(SampleID)
meta.0m<- meta.0m %>%
  arrange(SampleID)

#make sure no one is missing the outcome
table(is.na(meta.0m$outcome))
meta.0m[is.na(meta.0m$outcome)==F ,]
summary(meta.0m$outcome)

#see which IDs are not in both dataframes
setdiff(meta.0m$subject_id, meta.3m$subject_id)
setdiff(meta.3m$subject_id, meta.0m$subject_id)

#filter dataframes to only include IDs that are at both timepoints
common_ids <- intersect(meta.0m$subject_id, meta.3m$subject_id)

meta.0m_weight <- meta.0m %>% filter(subject_id %in% common_ids)
meta.3m_weight <- meta.3m %>% filter(subject_id %in% common_ids)

#confirm
#setdiff(meta.0m_weight$subject_id, meta.3m_weight$subject_id)
#setdiff(meta.3m_weight$subject_id, meta.0m_weight$subject_id)
```


### Running MiRKAT
```{r}
#filter your Aitchison DM to have the same IDs
Aitchison.0m<- Aitchison %>%
  dplyr::select(one_of(meta.0m_weight$SampleID)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(row.names(.) %in% meta.0m_weight$SampleID)%>%
  dplyr::arrange(row.names(.))

#confirm
#table(colnames(Aitchison.0m)==meta.0m_weight$SampleID)

#format the data
Aitchison.0m_matrix <- as.matrix(Aitchison.0m)
K.Aitchison.0m= D2K(Aitchison.0m_matrix) 
K.Aitchison.unifrac<- list(K.Aitchison.0m)

#create a set of covariates
covariates <- data.frame(
   age = meta.0m_weight$age   # etc.,            
   )


#?MiRKAT()
#MiRKAT(
#  y,   #this is your outcome
#  X = NULL,
#  Ks,  #this is the format Aitchison data
#  out_type = "C",  #this is either C for continuous (e.g., weight) or D for dichotomous (e.g., Y/N or 0/1)
#  method = "permutation",
#  nperm = 999,  #this is the default for method permutation, you do not need to include this line
#  returnKRV = T,  #default is FALSE, this is less important but can be included
#  returnR2 = T  #default is FALSE, but we want the R^2 value
#)


#fill in the function :)
wt <- MiRKAT()


```

```{r}
#generating a simple table

wt.df <- as.data.frame(wt)

rownames(wt.df)[1] = "Baseline - 3 months"
#can repeat for other timepoints, and use rbind() to put them into 1 table

knitr::kable(wt.df)
```
